comparator.name: Science, Technology & Innovation
comparator.academicYear: Current published UvA 2026–2027 bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official programme is 180 EC over three years. Year 1 lists twelve components totaling 60 EC across quantitative skills, digital methods, materials, life science, energy, food systems and professional research skills. The generic target requires a 54-EC year-2 specialisation; High-tech Designer Materials is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break, followed by the common 6-EC Design Project. Year 3 contains 30 EC genuine free choice, 12 EC Advanced Ethical Prototyping and an 18-EC Bachelor Project. The current page identifies the 2026–2027 digital study guide and explains that the bachelor project is three months of independent research recorded in a thesis.
components: Engineering the Building Blocks of Life
Genuine free-choice space; no particular minor or elective package is invented.
Independent three-month research project documented in a bachelor thesis.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names no specialisation. The official curriculum presents three equally substantial 54-EC year-2 tracks and does not establish one as the general route. High-tech Designer Materials appears first, so it is selected as a neutral tie-break independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Sustainable technology, materials & design
alternatives.concept: Combines broad natural-science and quantitative foundations with materials, energy, circularity, environmental systems, data, design and applied research to develop and evaluate sustainable technological solutions.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme is organised around sustainable technical systems, materials, quantitative analysis, design and applied research rather than claiming a dedicated engineering degree.
progression: Sustainability, programming, mathematics and environmental-science foundations precede systems analysis, circularity, modelling, resource recovery, renewable-system design and applied research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Digital modelling, robotics & prototyping
alternatives.concept: Emphasises programming, mathematics, data, modelling, simulation, software, robotics, optimisation and responsible prototype development, with product design and sustainability projects connecting digital models to physical solutions.
alternatives.labelReason: Programming, mathematical modelling, simulation, robotics and design form the visible spine, with both digital and physical prototype work.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces most earth, environmental, materials and circular-economy study with software development, computer vision, robotics, algorithms, reinforcement learning, optimisation and engineering mathematics. It differs by well over 30 EC and centres digital system design.
progression: Programming, data and mathematics foundations precede software, machine learning, modelling, computer vision, robotics, algorithms, optimisation, responsible design and project research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; ten 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Life, health & bioinnovation
alternatives.concept: Combines molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, physiology, laboratory science, health and disease with programming, data, quantitative methods, product design, sustainability and applied research for biotechnology and health-oriented innovation.
alternatives.labelReason: The programme visibly integrates life-science mechanisms and laboratory work with health applications, quantitative tools and innovation projects.
alternatives.distinctness: This route differs from the environmental/materials and digital-system programmes by replacing most geoscience, circular-systems and advanced computing content with molecular cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, laboratory work, anatomy, pharmacology, immunity and disease mechanisms. It passes the 30-EC distinctness floor against both earlier programmes.
progression: Life-science, programming, mathematics, data and sustainability foundations precede molecular biology, biochemistry, physiology, laboratory work, anatomy, pharmacology, genetics, immunity, disease, bioinnovation and applied research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

core: Applied integration of science, technology and innovation to address practical societal challenges
Engineering design, iterative prototyping, testing and technical feasibility analysis
Programming, data analysis, quantitative methods, scientific modelling and simulation
Broad natural-science foundations spanning materials, physics, chemistry, biology, biochemistry, energy and environmental systems
Research expertise, responsible innovation, collaboration, communication and evidence-based technology assessment
High-tech Designer Materials: structure, composition, properties and design of smart and functional materials
adjacent: Sustainability, circularity, renewable energy, life-cycle thinking and technical transition design
Digital modelling, simulation, robotics, electronics and computational prototype development
Engineering life and health through biotechnology, cell biology, biochemistry and biomedical applications
questions: How can materials, energy and environmental systems be designed for sustainability and circularity?
How can models, simulations and digital or physical prototypes test whether a technological solution will work?
How can biological and biochemical mechanisms be translated into useful health or biotechnology applications?

blocks: Science, materials, energy and sustainable systems
Both address material chemistry and properties, although UCR focuses on circular recovery and remediation.
Both integrate physics, chemistry, materials science and modelling around material behaviour.
Both address renewable-energy technology and technical system design.
Both require an applied research project with an external or practical scientific context; the UvA bachelor project is larger and individually thesis-based.
No selected UCR course provides a sufficiently direct one-to-one counterpart to the full Innovative Food Systems component.
Data, modelling, simulation and intelligent systems
The shared function is critical and responsible evaluation of advanced technological prototypes; the UvA component is broader and larger.
Both connect data handling and digital analysis to scientific applications.
Both introduce the digital and programming foundations used in later technical projects.
Both provide quantitative mathematical foundations for scientific analysis.
Both deepen quantitative skills needed for modelling and simulation.
Both introduce cellular, molecular and biochemical building blocks of living systems.
Both connect biochemical building blocks to practical life-science applications.
Design, responsible innovation and applied research
Both develop collaboration, reflection, communication and research-oriented professional skills.
Both centre iterative design work that develops a concrete product or prototype.
The UCR course develops evidence-based public communication and collaboration around climate and energy questions.
No selected UCR course provides a sufficiently direct one-to-one counterpart to the full Specialisation High-tech Designer Materials component.
No selected UCR course provides a sufficiently direct one-to-one counterpart to the full Open elective space component.

selection.assessment: The first programme is the closest feasible broad response to the selected materials-focused route while retaining the degree’s sustainability and design identity. Digital modelling/prototyping and life/health engineering are independently evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible directions that differ by well over 30 EC. A standalone Sustainability & Circularity route remains evidenced but is not attempted after reaching the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: UvA Science, Technology & Innovation combines dedicated makerspace prototyping, engineering projects and a 54-EC technical specialisation. UCR can assemble strong science, data, sustainability, product-design and research pathways, but it does not reproduce the same continuous engineering studio, materials laboratory or 54-EC named track. The UCR alternatives therefore show defensible related programmes, not professional engineering equivalence.
